name: Cel-Tech Communications, Inc. v. Los Angeles Cellular Telephone Co.
summary: The California Supreme Court held that courts must use a tethered, principled definition of 'unfair' business practices under the UCL to avoid giving courts unlimited power to remake business relationships based on their own policy preferences.
significance: Cited as the leading California Supreme Court decision defining the standard for 'unfair' conduct under the California UCL, which the lower courts applied in finding Apple's anti-steering policy unlawful.
